turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Hi, I'm Dr.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Haddad. Can you confirm your full name and date of birth for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thomas Kowaksic,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: May 3rd, 1981.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thanks, Thomas.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: You're walking a little carefully there. What happened?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, Saturday I was helping move pallets at work, and I picked up a box of floor tile wrong.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Twisted, you know,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: felt something grab in my lower back, right side.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Ouch.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Where do you work again? Harbor point distribution. I'm a shift laid in the warehouse.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Got it. On a scale of 0 to 10, how bad is the pain?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Right now, maybe a 6. When I bend over to tie my shoes, it's like an 8. Does it go anywhere, like down your leg? A little into the right butt cheek, not down the leg.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any numbness or tingling in your legs or feet. Any weakness, like your foot dragging.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, no numbness. Legs feel normal just the back. I have to ask a few important ones any numbness in the groin or between your legs like where you'd sit on a saddle No Any trouble controlling your bladder or bowels or trouble starting to pee? No, everything's working fine there any fevers unexplained weight loss or any history of cancer None of that Have you had back trouble before I had sciatica on the left side maybe six years ago Did physical therapy and it went away completely, haven't had it since. Good, what have you tried so far? Ibuprofen, two of the two hundreds a couple times a day, and my wife Agneska's heating pad. The heat helps some.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm kind of worried though,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: a guy on my crew herniated a disc doing the same thing and needed surgery.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's understandable. Let's take a look. Blood pressure is 134 over 84, pulse 76, temperature 98 .4. Can you stand and bend forward for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's about as far as I go.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, forward bending is limited by pain, about halfway. I can feel tight, tender muscles along the right side of your lower back. No tenderness when I press right on the spine itself. Now lie back.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm going to raise each leg straight. Just pulls in the back a little. Straight leg raise is negative on both sides.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Strength is normal in both legs, reflexes are equal at the knees and ankles,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: and you can feel my touch the same on both sides.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: You walked in normally, and you can walk on your heels and toes. So is it a disc? I don't think so. This looks like a strain of the muscles in your lower back. There are no warning signs, so you don't need an x -ray or MRI right now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Most of these get a lot better in two to four weeks. Okay, that's a relief.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: For pain, take ibuprofen 600mg 3 times a day with food for the next week or so. I'm also prescribing cyclobenzaprine, a muscle relaxer, 5mg at bedtime as needed for spasm. It can make you drowsy, so no driving or running the forklift after you take it.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Guard it only at night. Keep using heat and keep moving. Gentle walking is better than bed rest.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'll write you a note for light duty, no lifting over 20 pounds,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: through October 15th. My supervisor will want that, thanks.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: If you're not better in two weeks, come back and we'll start physical therapy. And if you ever lose control of your bladder or bowels, get numb between your legs, or a leg gets weak, go to the emergency room right away.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, Hopefully it doesn't come to that I don't expect it to let's plan a follow -up in two weeks. Take care of that back Thomas
